_scope: A PoE2-SHAPED DEMONSTRATION SLICE, hand-written for rtce's three sequencing examples (examples/poe2_charges.rs, poe2_poison.rs, poe2_triggers.rs). It is NOT Path of Exile 2's damage model and NOT derived from any game data: every coefficient here is `representative`, chosen so the examples' pins hand-derive in a comment. The real thing is ../poe2-calcs' GENERATED gamedef/poe2.gamedef.json (67 stats / 73 buckets / 209 pipeline stages / 80 objectives, emitted by that repo's `emit_gamedef` bin and pinned to its native `calc.rs` at 1e-9); its standing reference is 124.53 dps for a default Monk build. rtce cannot depend on poe2-calcs (the path dependency runs the other way), and a 209-stage pipeline is not hand-derivable, which is the whole reason this trimmed fixture exists. Note on `objectives`: `hit` and `poison_dps` are the two the examples actually drive (as `damage_objective`, and as a snapshot `tick_objective`). `phys_scaled` is listed as a third deliberately, though nothing reads it as an objective — it is the shared pre-mitigation magnitude the other two are both defined in terms of, and every hand-derivation in the three examples is written in terms of it. Naming it as an objective is what makes it queryable and visible in `Plan::explain()`, so a reader checking those derivations can SEE the intermediate instead of inferring it.
_shape: What is kept from PoE2's shape: two damage types with their own scaling chains (physical for the hit, chaos for the poison DoT); the two-tier `increased` (additive pool) / `more` (independent multiplier) split that is PoE2's signature; per-type enemy resistance with penetration; an ailment (shock) as a condition; and a DoT objective derived from the SAME pre-mitigation hit magnitude the hit uses, which is what makes an action-applied snapshot ailment inherit the applying hit's size. What is dropped: the other three elements, conversion, gain-as-extra, added-damage sources, minions, defences, and rate/cycle-time weighting.
_crit: Crit is CLOSED FORM here (`1 + c*(m-1)`), not an `events` branch — the same choice poe2-calcs' generated gamedef makes (its `events` block is empty). It is exact for this linear pipeline, and it means nothing in these slices samples, so EV and Monte Carlo agree to the bit and every pin is plain arithmetic. rtce's branched-event machinery is exercised by the Diablo 4 slice instead (tests/fixtures/d4/gamedef.json).
_hits_per_use: Deliberately NOT a stat here. `ActionDamage.stats`'s `hits_per_use` is read directly by the sim executor as the per-cast hit count and never reaches the Plan (see simdef::ActionDamage), so a `hit * hits_per_use` stage would silently read the BUILD's value instead of the casting action's. The D4 fixture carries it because its Level-1 `total_dps` objective is a per-second readout with no sim in the picture.
